# 

Task Description: Problem Statement Given are a prime number p and a sequence of p integers a_0, \ldots, a_{p-1} consisting of zeros and ones.
Find a polynomial of degree at most p-1, f(x) = b_{p-1} x^{p-1} + b_{p-2} x^{p-2} + \ldots + b_0, satisfying the following conditions:

For each i (0 <= i <= p-1), b_i is an integer such that 0 <= b_i <= p-1.
For each i (0 <= i <= p-1), f(i) \equiv a_i \pmod p.
Task Constraint: 2 <= p <= 2999
p is a prime number.
0 <= a_i <= 1
Task Input: Input is given from Standard Input in the following format:
p
a_0 a_1 \ldots a_{p-1}
Task Output: Print b_0, b_1, \ldots, b_{p-1} of a polynomial f(x) satisfying the conditions, in this order, with spaces in between.
It can be proved that a solution always exists. If multiple solutions exist, any of them will be accepted.
Task Samples: input: 2
1 0 output: 1 1

f(x) = x + 1 satisfies the conditions, as follows:

f(0) = 0 + 1 = 1 \equiv 1 \pmod 2
f(1) = 1 + 1 = 2 \equiv 0 \pmod 2
input: 3
0 0 0 output: 0 0 0

f(x) = 0 is also valid.
input: 5
0 1 0 1 0 output: 0 2 0 1 3

## Constraints
2 <= p <= 2999
p is a prime number.
0 <= a_i <= 1

## Input
Input is given from Standard Input in the following format:
p
a_0 a_1 \ldots a_{p-1}

## Output
Print b_0, b_1, \ldots, b_{p-1} of a polynomial f(x) satisfying the conditions, in this order, with spaces in between.
It can be proved that a solution always exists. If multiple solutions exist, any of them will be accepted.

## Examples
['input: 2\n1 0 output: 1 1\n\nf(x) = x + 1 satisfies the conditions, as follows:\n\nf(0) = 0 + 1 = 1 \\equiv 1 \\pmod 2\nf(1) = 1 + 1 = 2 \\equiv 0 \\pmod 2', 'input: 3\n0 0 0 output: 0 0 0\n\nf(x) = 0 is also valid.', 'input: 5\n0 1 0 1 0 output: 0 2 0 1 3']
